spec.description:
List all allocations for the user.

Requires the `Query Funds` API key permission.

By default all allocations are returned, even for strategies that have been used in the past and now have zero balance, so the user can see how much was earned with a given strategy historically. `hide_zero_allocations` removes zero-balance entries from the output. Paging hasn't been implemented for this method, as the result for a particular user isn't expected to be overwhelmingly large.

All amounts in the output can be denominated in a currency of the user's choice (the `converted_asset` parameter). Information about when the next reward will be paid is also provided.

Allocated funds can be in up to 4 states: `bonding`, `allocated`, `exit_queue` (ETH only), `unbonding`. Any funds in `total` not in `bonding`/`unbonding` are simply allocated and earning rewards; whether the other states also earn rewards depends on the strategy (see `Earn/Strategies`). ETH in `exit_queue` still earns rewards.

For ETH, when funds are in `exit_queue`, the `expires` time given is when the funds finish unbonding, not when they leave the exit queue for unbonding.

(Un)bonding time estimates can be inaccurate immediately after (de)allocating; wait 1-2 minutes for an accurate result.

ascending.description: `true` to sort ascending, `false` (the default) for descending.

converted_asset.description: A secondary currency to express the value of allocations in. Defaults to USD.

hide_zero_allocations.description: Omit entries for strategies used in the past that now hold no allocation. Defaults to `false`.

notes: `nonce` is dropped from the requestBody schema for the same reason as every other private Earn endpoint -- see `strategies/endpoint.json` notes.

Upstream's operation description states paging has not been implemented for this method ('we don't expect the result for a particular user to be overwhelmingly large'), and no `cursor`/`limit` request fields are documented at all. No `pagination` block is declared, per authoring rule 6.

Upstream's own worked example response includes a `next_cursor` field inside `result` that is not declared anywhere in the response `schema.properties` -- apparently copy-pasted from the sibling `Strategies` example, which does page. Omitted here since it is not a documented field of this endpoint's schema (rule 7 only requires keeping documented fields).

`amount_allocated`'s `bonding`/`exit_queue`/`pending`/`unbonding` sub-objects are independently-present optional fields of one object (each nullable, present only when that state has funds), not branches of a single discriminated field -- so they are modeled as ordinary nullable properties rather than an `anyOf`, per rule 4's own scope (unions of *shape*, not independently-optional fields).
